_note: Greenfield scenario for the unattended pipeline batch. All data is FICTIONAL sample data; no client data, code or vendor names. G2: student-facing UI.
feature: Student degree-progress dashboard: where I stand, what is left, and what to take next
problem: Students cannot see their degree progress in one place; they piece it together from transcripts and catalog pages, mostly on their phones
goals: Home page / lists three fictional sample students; choosing one opens /progress?student=<id>

Progress page: overall percent complete and credits earned of 120, one card per requirement group (General Education, Business Core, Major, Electives) with a progress bar, completed / in progress / remaining courses, and the credits each needs
A 'Take next' panel suggesting up to 5 eligible remaining courses whose prerequisites are complete, with the reason each is suggested
A what-if toggle: mark an in-progress course as failed and see the progress and suggestions change immediately

Polished, consistent visual design: a clear type scale, spacing system and colour palette defined once (CSS variables or a CSS module system), good contrast, focus styles; it must look like a product a university would ship, not unstyled HTML
Works on a phone (390 px wide) with no sideways scrolling, and on a desktop (1440 px) with a sensible max width
Accessible: semantic headings, labelled controls, progress bars with text equivalents, keyboard operable
Loading, empty and error states for every data view
non_goals: Real student data or any back-end integration (fictional in-memory data)

metrics.name: Time to answer 'what should I take next'

constraints: Next.js App Router with TypeScript; no UI framework is required, plain CSS modules are fine
Progress and suggestion logic is a pure, unit-tested module
